articles.title: Europa League: Lyon take down Crystal Palace, Cissè’s Milan hat-trick sinks Salzburg
articles.summary: Sage loses 3-2 to former side; Leverkusen go top. Alphadjo Cissè lights up 4-0 away victory. Crystal Palace’s Pierre Sage suffered a frustrating Europa League defeat as his side lost 3-2 to his former employers Lyon at the Groupama Stadium.
body: Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half void of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino cut the deficit in half five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the Ligue 1 side’s advantage. The Eagles substitute Daichi Kamada pulled one back with nine minutes remaining in a better second half for Palace, who could not find a third.

Days after beating his predecessor, the Nottingham Forest manager, Oliver Glasner, at Selhurst Park in the Premier League on Sunday, Sage found himself returning to the home of the club he managed for 14 months.
Ismaïla Sarr, who claimed the Conference League golden boot last season, was in a Crystal Palace starting lineup for the first time this season.

articles.title: Martínez apologises to Manchester United’s director of football Wilcox after outburst
articles.summary: Defender criticised technical director after loss in Madrid. Any disciplinary action will not be made public by club. Lisandro Martínez has apologised for claiming that Jason Wilcox, Manchester United’s director of football, failed to strengthen sufficiently in the summer window after discussions…
body: While any disciplinary action taken against him will not be made public by the club, it is thought Martínez has been fined.

The defender’s apology came on Thursday evening after the 28-year-old failed to offer one when issuing an initial statement on Wednesday regarding his outburst that came after Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League loss at Atlético Madrid.

He posted on Instagram: “Today I met with the club’s leadership and the manager. It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game.

“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”

articles.summary: Former QB says he is looking ‘for next landing spot’ Aikman and Buck said to have argued over contracts. Longtime Monday Night Football announcer Troy Aikman said he is looking for his “next landing spot” with ⁠his ESPN contract set to expire after February’s Super Bowl.
body: “I’ll broadcast through this season, and I’ll be ⁠a free agent ⁠at ​the end of the year and kind of see what happens,” Aikman said in a radio interview ⁠with KTCK of Dallas on Thursday morning.
Aikman, a Hall of Fame quarterback who won three Super Bowls with ⁠the Dallas Cowboys, is in the final year of a five-year deal ​with ESPN that pays him $18m ‌annually.

Joe Buck, Aikman’s ‌broadcast partner for the past 25 years, recently finalized a six-year extension ‌with ESPN that is worth more than $100m, according to the Athletic. Buck’s deal runs through the network’s next Super Bowl broadcast in 2031.

In Thursday’s radio interview, Aikman appeared to confirm earlier reports from Front Office Sports that there was tension between ‌him and Buck over their contract situations. The pair reportedly had an argument before Monday’s game between the ​Buffalo Bills and Los Angeles Rams.

articles.title: Chelsea are the Premier League’s most fun team but is it sustainable?
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso’s side are scoring and conceding at a remarkable rate. It’s great for neutrals but not necessarily the best way to qualify for Europe. By WhoScored. Watching Chelsea this season ought to come with a health warning.
body: They have scored 15 goals from an expected goals total of just 8.4, an over-performance of 6.6. An 18.3% conversion rate is second only to Manchester City’s 19.1%, while eight of their 15 goals have come from shots with xG below 0.13. The five goals against Bournemouth last weekend came from an xG of just 0.75.

Cole Palmer, João Pedro and Morgan Rogers complement each other’s qualities. Palmer’s instinct to drift into pockets of space and dictate attacks gives Chelsea a creative focal point; Rogers provides the direct running and ball-carrying to unsettle defences; and João Pedro offers the movement to stretch opponents in behind and the composure to finish when chances arrive. They rotate roles too, giving defenders a constant headache – they can’t crowd out one of the trio without giving another space.

articles.title: Serb player banned until 2050 for tennis match-fixing
articles.summary: Stefan Milicevic is given a 24-year suspension from tennis - one of the most severe punishments outside of a lifetime ban - for match-fixing.
body: Stefan Milicevic, who reached a career-high world ranking of 1,338th in 2014, was charged with fixing six matches, including five in which he was competing.
The 29-year-old, who played on the lower rungs of the professional ladder, was also charged with attempting to fix a further six matches between 2022 and 2024.

Along with the match-fixing, the International Tennis Integrity Authority (ITIA) said Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players "as part of a corrupt network".
Players who were recruited by Milicevic have also been accused by the ITIA of fixing matches.

articles.summary: The NBA released its annual survey of its general managers on Oct. 15, and one Milwaukee Bucks player was at the top of their list when it came to the question of " which rookie was the biggest steal at where he was selected in the draft?
body: A whopping 30% of the league's top decision-makers picked Brayden Burries as that "steal," placing him far and away ahead of Toronto's Allen Graves, Philadelphia's Labaran Philon and Cleveland's Meleek Thomas. Each of those rookies received 10% of the vote.
Burries was picked No. 10 by the Buck s out of the University of Arizona. Graves (No. 19) and Philon (No. 22) were picked later in the first round and Thomas (No. 34) was a second-round selection.

The Bucks' second pick in the draft, Nate Ament, also received votes in the survey. Ament was originally drafted by Miami at No. 13 but was selected for Milwaukee as part of the Giannis Antetokounmpo trade.

articles.title: British Cycling to act after 'toxic' survey responses
articles.summary: British Cycling is to launch an "action plan" following a survey in which some responses reportedly described its World Class Programme as "toxic".
body: The confidential survey was funded by UK Sport and carried out by an independent company earlier this year.

The Times reported, external that the results found there was a drop in morale among riders and performance staff, while "toxic" was the joint-second most common response to a question asking for words to describe the programme.
"The wellbeing of our staff and riders is fundamental to everything we do at British Cycling," said a British Cycling spokesperson.
"The Culture Feedback Survey, which has been the subject of recent reports, is independently run to provide a valuable tool to help us learn and improve.

articles.summary: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology for his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid.
body: Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Spain, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad and said he expected more from "upstairs" after he singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.
Sky Sports News understands Martinez met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, on Thursday. Head coach Michael Carrick was also present at the meeting.
In a statement released on Thursday night, the defender said: "Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager.
"It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

articles.title: J.T. Realmuto plan leaves door open for Phillies to make splash in free agency
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Phillies could have a new path to upgrading their roster after J.T. Realmuto acknowledged that he needs to improve offensively and could play some first base next season. MORE: Phillies to hire former Mets coach in drastic shakeup.
body: According to NBC Sports Philadelphia’s John Clark, Realmuto told president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski, that he needs to get better at the plate. He also said the mental demands of catching have left him feeling drained, although he feels good physically.
Giving Realmuto more days away from the plate could help manage that workload while opening the door for Philadelphia to pursue another catcher, including Minnesota Twins backstop Ryan Jeffers.
Jeffers has previously emerged as a potential target for Philadelphia. Sports Illustrated reported that the Phillies explored him as an option while considering alternatives behind the plate.

Acquiring Jeffers would likely require a trade rather than a straightforward free-agent signing, depending on his contractual status. He could give the Phillies another established catcher while allowing Realmuto to play first base occasionally or receive additional rest.

articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out of their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday due to a blood clot in his calf.
body: The Eagles said in a statement on Thursday that Hurts was injured in their Week Four defeat to the Los Angeles Rams on October 4 when he took a boot to his calf area, which led to the discovery of the clot.
The Super Bowl 59 MVP practised on Friday last week, before the team left for London to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Hurts played the full game against the Jags, completing 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown in a 19-17 loss, and the Eagles confirmed he practised in the first half of this week before an ultrasound on Wednesday revealed "movement in the small blood clot".

"Out of an abundance of caution, an ultrasound was performed on Saturday following the team's flight to London and walkthrough," the Eagles explained in their statement. "The ultrasound revealed a superficial blood clot.

articles.title: Can Van Gerwen end his barren spell at Dutch Darts Championship?
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen will look to end his barren run with victory at the Elten Safety Shoes Dutch Darts Championship, with the draw and schedule now confirmed.
body: The three-time world champion endured a disappointing first-round exit at the World Grand Prix against Ryan Joyce before suffering another early setback with a second-round defeat to Mensur Suljovic at last weekend's Swiss Darts Trophy.

With the final European Tour event of 2026 taking place at MECC Maastricht from October 16-18, the race for European Championship qualification reaches its climax on Dutch soil, with 'The Green Machine' determined to end his title drought in front of his home crowd.
Van Gerwen's last big tournament success came at the Nordic Darts Masters in June, where he defeated Luke Humphries in the final.
His last major TV title before that came on home soil at the 2025 World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
